title: Integrate FP8/INT8 quant benchmarks into perf-canary + add regression thresholds/allowlists
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Goal
- Add FP8/INT8 quant benchmark runs to perf-canary (nightly) on a small, stable matrix of (model family x GPU SKU x quant mode), and gate the release train on defined regression thresholds.

Why
- We’re landing multiple changes in the quantized path (kernel tuning, auto-selection fixes, scheduler knobs). We need an automated signal that catches perf regressions (TTFT/TPOT + throughput) and identifies kernel-selection mismatches early.

Scope
1) New perf-canary job(s)
- A dedicated “quant-perf” canary that runs nightly, plus an on-demand workflow for release candidates.
- Target GPUs (initial): H100 + A100 (add H200/L40S once lab capacity is stable).
- Target models/workloads: use benchmark-lab presets for top hosted chat; include streaming chat scenario (TTFT/TPOT) + one non-streaming throughput scenario.

2) Result ingestion + tagging
- Enforce standard metadata tags in artifacts so regressions can be attributed:
  - quant_mode (fp8|int8|fp16 baseline)
  - chosen_kernel_id / kernel_family
  - model_family, model_id, runtime_commit, container_digest
  - gpu_sku, driver/cuda version, clocks mode

3) Regression thresholds + gating policy
- Define thresholds and when to block:
  - Blockers: p95 TTFT regression beyond threshold on streaming chat; or tokens/sec regression beyond threshold on throughput case.
  - Warn-only: p50 regressions; p99 noise above known variance bands.
- Add allowlists for known exceptions (per GPU, per model, per quant mode) with an expiry + owner.
- Add robust stats / outlier handling and minimum run count.

4) Notifications + debuggability
- Slack notification to #eng-runtime with: diff summary, links to artifacts, and “top suspected changes” (based on runtime commit range and kernel-selection events).
- Make it easy to repro locally in perf-lab with the exact pinned config.

Acceptance criteria
- A nightly perf-canary run produces a pass/fail for quant perf across the selected matrix and posts a summary.
- Thresholds are written down in policy (linked ADR / Confluence) and implemented in the comparator.
- Allowlist mechanism exists and is auditable (who/why/expiry).
- A failing run includes enough metadata to identify: (a) which phase regressed (prefill vs decode), (b) whether kernel auto-selection changed, (c) whether GPU clocks / contention likely changed.

Non-goals
- Not expanding to full benchmark matrix; canary should stay small and stable.

Links
- Perf-canary PR: sources/github/perf-canary/pr_188.json (new quant-perf job)
- Perf-canary PR: sources/github/perf-canary/pr_189.json (comparator robustness)
- Harness support: benchmark-lab schema + artifacts (PRs 412–415)
- Kernel logging spans: redwood PR 10621 (needed for attribution)

Open questions
- What’s the initial threshold per metric per SKU (A100 vs H100)? We may need different bands.
- Do we gate on absolute p95 or relative delta vs last-good? (proposal below in comments)
comments:
2025-10-02 (Sahana Iyer): Implemented quant-perf canary job wiring in perf-canary branch. Using benchmark-lab preset: streaming_chat_e2e + throughput_nonstreaming. Pinned runtime commit + container digest pulled from benchmark-lab config. Next: comparator thresholds + allowlist format.

Proposed initial metrics (per run):
- Streaming chat: TTFT_p95_ms, TPOT_p95_ms, prefill_ms_p95, decode_ms_p95
- Throughput: tokens_per_sec_mean, tokens_per_sec_p95

Proposed gating: fail if TTFT_p95 or tokens/sec regresses > X% relative to last-good baseline on same SKU + quant_mode. Need agreement on X% (see ENG-24810 success criteria thread).

Dependencies: requires kernel-selection event export for better attribution (redwood PR 10621); currently only have coarse tags from benchmark-lab metadata.

2025-10-04 (Connor O'Brien): +1 to relative gating vs last-good. For release train, also want a hard absolute guardrail (TTFT p95 < N ms) to catch baseline drift when last-good is already bad. Suggest:
- Relative fail: > 7% TTFT_p95 regression, > 5% tokens/sec regression (H100). Slightly looser on A100 (variance).
- Absolute warn: TTFT_p95 > 900ms on streaming case (H100). Adjust once we have 1 week of data.

Allowlist needs: owner + expiry (<= 14 days) + link to issue. Please enforce in code so it can’t become permanent.

Also: route Slack notifications to #eng-runtime, @oncall-runtime only for hard fails.

2025-10-06 (Allison Grant): For dashboards/alert triage, please ensure tags include model_family + quant_mode + gpu_sku + runtime_version. We can auto-link to the dashboard panel with those query params. If possible, add a small ‘likely cause’ section in Slack message: kernel selection change? scheduler policy change? clocks changed?

If kernel ids aren’t available yet, at least include shapes and quant path (fp8/int8).

2025-10-08 (Sahana Iyer): Landed comparator changes with robust stats + outlier trimming behind flag (paired with perf-canary PR 189). Implemented allowlist YAML with required fields:
- reason
- owner
- expires_at
- tracking_issue

Enforced: run fails if allowlist entry is expired.

Also added minimum samples = 5, and ‘noise floor’ check to avoid failing on <1% deltas.

Known issue: perf-lab contention causing false positives (queue wait spikes) on A100. I added a temporary allowlist entry (expires 2025-10-15, owner: Sean Gallagher) while perf-lab isolation work continues. Tracking in INT-842 + ENG-24812.

Requesting review from Connor + Noah.

2025-10-10 (Noah Patel): Reviewed the comparator logic. Looks good overall. One tweak requested: for streaming, gate on TPOT_p95 in addition to TTFT_p95; TTFT only catches prefill but we’ve seen decode regressions from scheduler batch caps. Suggest fail if either TTFT_p95 regresses > threshold OR TPOT_p95 regresses > threshold.

Also request: Slack output should include prefill/decode breakdown deltas so we can immediately route to kernels vs scheduler.

Once addressed, approve for merge and enable in nightly.
